Short answer: Yes — as of today (September 4, 2026) Ireland’s standard VAT rate is 23%, and that standard rate is what normally applies to digital services supplied to Irish consumers. ([revenue.ie](https://www.revenue.ie/en/vat/vat-rates/search-vat-rates/current-VAT-rates.aspx?utm_source=openai))

A couple of quick notes:
- Revenue’s official “Current VAT rates” table shows the standard rate at 23% (published 1 Jan 2026). ([revenue.ie](https://www.revenue.ie/en/vat/vat-rates/search-vat-rates/current-VAT-rates.aspx?utm_source=openai))  
- Some supplies (e.g., certain hospitality items, hairdressing) have reduced rates (13.5% or the 9% rate introduced for specific items from 1 July 2026), but those reduced rates don’t typically apply to digital services. ([gov.ie](https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-finance/speeches/speech-by-minister-paschal-donohoe-on-the-second-stage-of-the-finance-bill/?utm_source=openai))

If you’d like, I can:
- Draft a short line to replace or append in your pricing PDF (including a citation and “checked as of Sept 4, 2026”), or  
- Edit the PDF text for you if you upload it. Which would you prefer?
